newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat after bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat after bargain-hunting.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were broadly unchanged in late trade on Friday, as prices remained fixed around the week's lows and bargain-hunting was not sufficient to spark a rebound.
"I've got dollar bonds unchanged to up an eighth of a point, high-grades unchanged," a municipal analyst said, noting activity was light.

This week's approximately 15-basis point rise in yields, which was kicked off by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's warning that he would launch a pre-emptive strike against inflation, if necessary, aided bottom-feeders.

For example, a trader said that Maryland's sale of $240 million of general obligation bonds, which this morning had an unsold balance of nearly $78 million, were moved at 10 basis points below the offering price in the 2004 to 2008 maturities. This was about level with trades seen on Thursday for the 2002 maturity, he said, adding: "They had a decent distribution of the bonds."

Bonds sold by the Municipal Assistance Corporation for New York City, which in the teeth of the falling market on Wednesday sold $465 million of debt, were offered about five basis points lower on Friday, the trader said. The issues were repriced that day, with the top yield in 1008 lifted five basis points to 5.05 percent.

Looking ahead to next week, the market was bracing for a series of economic reports that culiminate with the release on Friday of the crucial payrolls data for February. "That could be when they (the Federal Reserve) tightens," a trader speculated. "If it's a real strong number, who knows?"

U.S. payrolls were predicted to fall to 230,000 from 271,000 in January, according to a Reuters consensus survey of economists, while the unemployment rate was expected to ease one percentage point to 5.3 percent.

And at least one municipal analyst suggested that the Federal Reserve now might have less maneuvering room, following his latest comments, as the market could sell-off if the central bank failed to tighten rates.

"After Greenspan's uncharacteristically blunt expression of concern, it is possible that the markets would react negatively if the Fed did not raise short-term rates. The burden of proof has shifted so that now the question is whether forthcoming economic statistics will provide enough evidence of moderation to support a decision to leave rates unchanged," said Nuveen Research, in its market comments.
Supplies for next week, though bigger than first anticipated, only added up to about $2.8 billion in 73 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Negotiated offerings total $2.1 billion in 33 sales, the biggest a $300 million Jefferson County, Ala., issue through Raymond James. On the competitive side, 40 sales totaling $746 million are on the schedule. A $450 million North Carolina deal on Wednesday is the largest.

March U.S. Treasury bond futures on the Chicago Board of Trade rose seven ticks to 116-1/32, while the March municipal bond futures gained five ticks to end at 110-29/32. This put the MOB spread at plus 164 ticks.
Metropolitan Pier & Exposition Authority Illinois Dedicated State Tax Revenues Refundings of June 2027, which carry a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were offered at 5.72 percent, NET, up four basis points.
And Denver Colorado City and County Airport Revenues of November 2025, which have a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were offered at 5.76 percent, NET, unchanged.
